title: Async connection-pool draining and multi-region circuit escrow for graceful degradation
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: During regional downstream outages (Redis / Kafka / SQL), our current connection pools either block callers while waiting for backends or immediately drop requests with a blunt 5xx. This produces amplified tail latency, increased client retries, and customer-visible errors despite available alternative regions and degraded read-only variants.

Goal: Implement an async drain + "escrow" token approach for per-region connection pools, paired with a persistent circuit state (escrowed circuits) that allows in-flight requests to complete, favors fast local fallbacks, and enables controlled load shedding with SLO-aware thresholds. The implementation should integrate with smart routing so traffic can be moved proactively and safely to fallback regions or to read-only caches without causing cascading failures.

Scope: 1) Async connection acquisition with soft deadlines and escrow tokens that can be revoked for rapid shedding. 2) Circuit state persisted in a small regional metadata store so failover decisions survive process restarts and are observable across nodes. 3) Two-level degradation: conservative (serve from local cache/KV with staleness bound) and aggressive (route to fallback region or return synthetic 503 with retry-advice). 4) Instrumentation + dashboards and an automated chaos test to validate goals.

Links: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/async-connpool-drain ; perf dash (staging): https://dash.redwood.ai/r/connpool-drain-staging ; early PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5289
acceptance_criteria: Per-region pool can revoke escrow tokens and reduce active acquisition rate within 50ms after circuit open signal.

During simulated downstream latency spike (90th->99th percentile increased by 10x), overall 95th percentile latency for API generation routes does not exceed SLO by more than 20% compared to baseline with simulated failover to fallback region enabled.
Failover exercises show <150ms median additional routing latency when switching to fallback region for 99% of requests during controlled test window.
Circuit state persists across process restarts and is visible in the Console rollout dashboard; ops can manually force-open/close a circuit for a region.
Automated chaos experiment reproduces graceful drain: no request is dropped silently—either served, retried, or returned with structured retry-advice and error-code for clients.
Unit and integration tests cover token escrow lifecycle, revocation, and fallback routing logic; PR has at least two approving reviews and one perf sign-off.
notes: Trade-offs: escrow tokens avoid blocking callers but add bookkeeping overhead per request; we will batch token reconciliation to reduce CPU cost.
We chose small regional metadata store (embedded raft lite) instead of global control plane updates to minimize cross-region write latency.
Fallback routing will respect customer pinning — customers with 'pin_region' will see a more conservative policy and may be routed to a read-only variant instead of cross-region route.

Edge-case: Kafka consumer groups need special handling — we will not automatically switch consumer leader region; instead we surface an operator action and provide a read-through proxy for short windows.
